about: ABYSSAL LANTERN is a deep-sea survival roguelite for the make.fun best-game-01 bounty. You are Neria, the last lanternfish, guarding the Abyssal Garden. Survive five minutes against an escalating swarm, gather the light of fallen enemies, level up and draft your build, and slay the Leviathans that rise at 90 and 210 seconds. Win by surviving 5:00; lose when your light goes out. This document is the game's design record: what every system does, why it is tuned the way it is, and how to play it well. It ships with the game so the dossier carries the full design, not just the code.

faq.can_i_pause: Yes — P or Esc. The pause screen shows your current build. The game also pauses itself while the level-up draft is open.
faq.do_i_need_the_mouse: Only to aim the Sun Harpoon. Every other weapon fires on its own. If you never move the mouse, the harpoon aims at the nearest enemy, so the game is fully playable on keyboard alone.
faq.how_do_i_lose: Your HP bar (top-left) reaching zero. Contact with an enemy costs HP (reduced by armor, minimum 1), ink shots cost 10, and the Leviathan's contact costs 20. There is no other fail state — the clock only ever helps you.
faq.how_do_i_win: Survive 300 seconds. The timer at the top counts down from 5:00; at zero the Garden blooms and the run ends in victory. You do not need to kill the Leviathans to win, but they drop 40 XP and a pearl each, so killing them is almost always worth it.
faq.is_the_game_random: Every run is seeded from the clock, so spawns, drafts and enemy mixes differ each time. The wave schedule and the boss times (90s, 210s) are fixed, so a run is fair: the same skill wins the same way.
faq.what_happens_when_i_level_up: The game pauses and offers three cards: a new weapon, an upgrade to a weapon you own, or a stat boon. Pick one with the mouse or keys 1/2/3. If you earned two levels at once (a boss kill can do that), a second draft opens right after the first.
faq.what_if_i_close_the_tab: The run ends. Runs are not saved — a run is five minutes, and the score is the record.

playtest_notes.balance_observation: The pulse ray alone nearly keeps up with wave-2 spawning (29 kills in 35 seconds), which is the intended gentle opening. The pressure test is waves 5-8, where the spawn cap (39-54) exceeds any single weapon's clear rate and the draft choices decide the run.
playtest_notes.bugs_found_and_fixed: Three bugs were found by reading the screenshots, not by the error log: (1) the title scene staged the world but never showed the title overlay (boot hid all screens for shot runs); (2) the ambient drifters were simulated but never drawn; (3) the HUD showed through the title screen. All three were fixed and the shots re-taken.
playtest_notes.headless_autopilot_16_nov: A 40-second headless autopilot (wandering WASD, periodic dashes, first-card draft picks) finished at score 1,093, level 2, 34 kills, wave 2, with 1 level-up drafted and 0 JavaScript errors. The timer read 4:20, exactly 40 seconds in, confirming the fixed 60 Hz timestep tracks real time.
playtest_notes.screenshot_scenes: All four staged scenes render with 0 errors: the cover (wave 6, boss at 62% HP, combo x8), the title (menu over a living backdrop), the level-up draft (three cards including a new weapon), and the results screen (8 final stats, restart button).

sound_design.approach: All sound is synthesized with the WebAudio API — oscillators, noise buffers and gain envelopes, no audio files. Fifteen effects cover shots, hits, kills, pickups, level-ups, dashes, boss spawns, the win and the loss. The combo sound rises in pitch with the chain, so the player hears the multiplier climbing.
sound_design.mute: M or the speaker button toggles sound. Audio starts only after the first click or keypress, as browsers require, so the title screen is silent until the player dives in.
sound_design.why_synth: No audio files means no downloads, no licensing, and no load failure: the game is a single static folder that works offline. The synth also lets effects respond to the game (combo pitch, boss depth) in ways fixed samples cannot.

accessibility: The game is fully playable by keyboard alone except for harpoon aiming, which falls back to the nearest enemy when the mouse has not moved. Sound is optional (M toggles it) and every sound has a visual counterpart (damage numbers, flashes, banners). Text is high-contrast on dark panels, and the HUD uses shape and colour together (bars plus numbers) rather than colour alone.
balancing_notes: Numbers were set by reasoning from the win condition, not by feel alone. The player needs roughly 4,000 damage per minute by wave 8 to hold the field; the five weapons at level 3 output about 5,200 damage per minute between them, so a player who drafts evenly wins with margin and a player who drafts badly (all boons, one weapon) loses around wave 7 — which is the intended skill gap. The Leviathan's 900 HP at 90s takes about 25 seconds of focused level-3 fire, which is long enough to feel like a boss and short enough that the fight does not outlast the wave. The dash cooldown (2.2s) is longer than a darter lunge cycle, so the dash is a decision, not a reflex.

controls.1_2_3_or_click: Pick a level-up card when the draft opens. The game pauses while the draft is open, so there is no time pressure on the choice.
controls.M: Toggle sound. Sound is synthesized WebAudio (no audio files) and starts muted until the first click or keypress, as browsers require.
controls.P_or_Esc: Pause. The pause screen shows the current build so the player can review it mid-run.
controls.R: Restart from an end screen (or from pause). A fresh run starts at once.
controls.WASD_or_arrows: Swim. Movement is acceleration-based (600 px/s^2) with friction, so the fish glides and turns with weight; the top speed is 230 px/s, raised by the Swift Fin boon and the Tide Caller's Gift.
controls.mouse: Aims the Sun Harpoon only. All other weapons are automatic (nearest enemy, or ambient). The harpoon fires toward the mouse pointer, so the player steers damage with the mouse while steering the fish with the keyboard.
controls.space: Dash: a 0.18s burst at 3.1x speed in the current movement direction (or facing direction if still), with a 2.2s cooldown and brief invulnerability while dashing. The dash bar at bottom-right fills as it recharges and glows when ready. Dash through a pack to escape, or through a boss's radial burst to dodge it.

bulwark.counterplay: Focus fire. The harpoon and the storm are the efficient answers; the pulse ray alone takes too long. Bulwarks are slow, so kiting past them is always an option — but they will still be there when you come back.
bulwark.role: The tank. A walking reef that absorbs fire and holds the player's attention while the swarm closes in.
bulwark.stats: HP 70, speed 38 px/s, contact 12, 4 XP, 40 score.

darter.counterplay: The lunge is telegraphed: the darter pauses and flashes before it bursts. Sidestep the line, or dash through it. Darters are the reason the dash has invulnerability.
darter.role: The lunger. It drifts slowly, then bursts at the player in a fast lunge.
darter.stats: HP 18, cruise 55 px/s, lunge 340 px/s, contact 8, 2 XP, 20 score.

elites.counterplay: Elites are a risk/reward choice: they take three times the fire to kill, but they pay double XP and are worth the focus fire if the field is otherwise clear. If the field is crowded, kite them — they are slow enough to ignore for a while.
elites.role: From wave 4 onward, 10% of spawns (12% from wave 6) are elites: 3x HP, 1.25x size, 2x XP, and a gold ring.

gloomlet.counterplay: Anything kills a gloomlet. The danger is never one gloomlet; it is twenty of them arriving at once while a bulwark holds the line. Keep moving so they string out instead of balling up.
gloomlet.role: The basic chaser. Slow, weak, numberless — the swarm's filler.
gloomlet.stats: HP 12, speed 62 px/s, contact 6, 1 XP, 10 score.

leviathan.counterplay: Stay at medium range and circle: the radial burst is dodgeable by dashing through a gap, and the Leviathan is too slow to catch a moving player. Bring the harpoon — it is the only weapon with the single-target damage to end the fight quickly. Slaying a Leviathan drops a pearl (vacuum) and 40 XP, usually a full level.
leviathan.role: The boss. Arrives at 90s and again at 210s, with a boss health bar and a radial ink burst every few seconds.
leviathan.stats: HP 900 (first) / 1400 (second), speed 46 px/s, contact 20, radial burst of 10 ink shots, 40 XP, 500 score, drops a pearl.

spitter.counterplay: Ink shots are slow and dodgeable — keep moving perpendicular to the spitter. The harpoon outranges it; the orbs cannot reach it. Spitters punish players who sit still and let the swarm come to them.
spitter.role: The ranged harasser. It keeps about 280 px of distance and spits ink shots that travel in straight lines.
spitter.stats: HP 22, speed 66 px/s, contact 8, ink shot 10 damage, 3 XP, 30 score.

splitter.counterplay: Kill it at range, then kill the children before they scatter — or kill it on a mine so the burst takes the whole family. The storm's chains are ideal: they jump to the children as they spawn.
splitter.role: The multiplier. On death it splits into two gloomlets, so a kill becomes two new threats.
splitter.stats: HP 30, speed 70 px/s, contact 8, 3 XP, 30 score (plus the children's XP).

overview.difficulty: The opening 30 seconds are gentle (gloomlets only, a slow trickle) so a first-time player learns to swim and gather. Pressure ramps on a fixed schedule: darters at 30s, bulwarks at 60s, splitters at 90s, spitters at 120s, the first Leviathan at 90s and the second at 210s. Enemy HP and speed scale 5% per 15 seconds after 60s, and the spawn cap rises from 14 to 60. A player who stands still dies in the first minute; a player who keeps moving and drafts damage wins with room to spare.
overview.goal: Survive 300 seconds. The timer counts down from 5:00 at the top of the screen; when it reaches zero the Garden blooms and the run ends in victory. Every other number — score, level, kills, best combo — is a measure of how well the run went, not a second win condition.
overview.loop: Swim with WASD or the arrow keys. Weapons fire on their own — the player's job is positioning, dodging and choosing. Slain enemies drop light-gems; gathering gems fills the XP bar; each level opens a draft of three cards (new weapon, weapon upgrade, or stat boon); the build grows until the run ends. Waves rise every 30 seconds, the abyss shifts tier every 60 seconds, and bosses arrive on schedule.
overview.session_length: One run is exactly five minutes of play plus menus. A run that ends early ends early; a run that wins ends at 5:00. The game is built to be replayed: the draft is random, the spawns are seeded per run, and the score rewards aggressive play.

pickups.kelp: Heals 25 HP. Drops from bulwarks (25% chance) and splitters (15%).
pickups.pearl: Vacuums every gem on the field into the player at once. Drops from elites (35%), bulwarks (12%), and always from a Leviathan. A pearl at the right moment — just after a big clear — is worth a whole level.

progression.combo: Kills within 2.5 seconds of each other chain a combo, up to x8. Score per kill is multiplied by the combo, so aggressive clearing pays more than cautious kiting. The combo meter shows above the score; losing the chain is silent, building it is loud (the combo sound rises in pitch).
progression.draft: Each level offers 3 cards drawn without replacement, weighted: weapon upgrades 3, new weapons 2, stat boons 2. The draft never offers a weapon already at level 5, and never offers a 6th weapon (the arsenal caps at 5, one per weapon). If everything is maxed, the draft offers a heal and a score card instead, so a level is never wasted.
progression.stat_boons: Eight boons, each stackable: Vitality (+20 max HP and heal 20), Swift Fin (+12% move speed), Magnet (+40% pickup radius), Thick Scales (+1 armor, reducing every hit), Sharp Teeth (+15% damage), Rapid Fin (+10% fire rate), Lucky Lure (+8% crit chance), Second Wind (heal 30% of max HP now). Armor applies per hit with a minimum of 1 damage, so it shines against gloomlet swarms and matters little against the Leviathan — a deliberate trade-off.
progression.xp_curve: Level N needs 8 + (N-1) * 6 XP (level 2 needs 8, level 10 needs 62, level 20 needs 122). Gems are worth 1 XP each (2 from elites, 40 from a boss), so the early levels come fast and the late levels need real clearing.

scoring.kills: 10 (gloomlet), 20 (darter), 40 (bulwark), 30 (splitter), 30 (spitter), 500 (leviathan), all multiplied by the current combo (x1 to x8).
scoring.pickups: Gems are worth 1 score each, pearls 25, kelp 10.
scoring.win_bonus: Surviving to 5:00 adds 1,000 score. A strong winning run lands around 25,000–35,000; a run that dies at 3:00 lands around 12,000–18,000.

strategy_guide: Move constantly. The swarm is slow; the player is fast. A player who never stops moving takes almost no contact damage in the first two minutes. The most common beginner mistake is standing still to watch the weapons fire.

Draft damage early, survivability late. The first three drafts should be weapons and damage boons (Sharp Teeth, Rapid Fin) — the faster the swarm dies, the fewer gems are left behind and the faster the next level comes. Vitality and Thick Scales matter from wave 5 onward, when the field is dense enough to hit back.

The harpoon is the boss answer. If a Leviathan is due in the next 30 seconds, take or upgrade the Sun Harpoon. The pulse ray and the storm clear packs; only the harpoon ends a boss fight before the second radial burst.
Save the dash for the lunge. Darters telegraph; the dash's invulnerability window is exactly long enough to pass through a lunge. Dashing on cooldown wastes the one escape that cannot be hit.

Chain the combo. The x8 multiplier is worth more than any single weapon upgrade. After a big clear, chase the stragglers for two seconds to keep the chain alive — the score difference over a run is thousands.

Use the pearl after a clear, not before. A pearl vacuums the gems already on the field, so it is worthless on an empty field and worth a level on a full one. If a pearl drops mid-fight, leave it until the wave thins, then grab it.
Kite the bulwarks, kill the spitters. Bulwarks are slow and can be ignored; spitters force movement and punish standing still. The harpoon's pierce kills a spitter through the pack in front of it.

Mines are a route, not a weapon. Drop them along the line you are about to run, not where you are standing. A minefield behind a fleeing player is free damage; a mine under a standing player is a wasted slot.

The Leviathan's radial burst has gaps. The 10 shots are evenly spaced, so there is always a lane between two of them. Dash through a gap, or simply step sideways — the shots are slow enough to walk around.

Watch the tier, not the clock. Each tier shift is a 60-second marker: when the water turns violet, the first Leviathan is 30 seconds away; when it turns magenta, the second is 30 seconds away. Draft accordingly.
systems_summary: Twelve source files, one job each: random (seeded RNG), config (all tuning), input (keyboard/mouse), audio (WebAudio synth), particles (juice), world (state and economy), player (movement and gems), enemies (six types + boss AI), weapons (five weapons), upgrades (draft), waves (schedule), render (canvas), hud (DOM), shots (screenshot scenes), main (loop and state machine). The fixed 60 Hz timestep keeps the simulation identical at any display refresh rate. The game runs offline from static files; there is no network, no build step, and no dependency beyond the browser.
title: ABYSSAL LANTERN — design document, mechanics guide and strategy guide

waves_and_tiers.boss_schedule: Leviathans arrive at 90s and 210s, each announced by a banner and a deep sound. A second Leviathan never spawns while the first still lives, so the boss fights stay fair.
waves_and_tiers.spawn_cap: The cap rises from 14 (wave 1) to 60 (wave 10+): 14 + wave * 5, capped at 60. Continuous spawning keeps the field at the cap, so the pressure is constant rather than bursty.
waves_and_tiers.tiers: Every 60 seconds the abyss shifts tier: Twilight Reach (blue), the Murk (teal), Violet Deep (purple), the Ember Cracks (magenta), and the Black Garden (near-black with gold light). Each tier changes the background gradient, the fog colour and the ambient particles, so the player can feel the clock without reading it.
waves_and_tiers.waves: A new wave every 30 seconds, announced by a banner ('WAVE 3' with a chime). Each wave unlocks a new enemy type on schedule and raises the spawn cap, so the field gets denser and more varied at the same time.

abyss_storm.role: Chain lightning that arcs between nearby enemies — the swarm melter.
abyss_storm.stats: Level 1: 12 damage, 4 chains, 1.1 strikes/s. Level 5: 30 damage, 10 chains, 2.2 strikes/s.
abyss_storm.strategy: The strongest weapon against dense packs: each strike jumps to the nearest unhit enemy within 260 px, so a tight swarm takes the full chain. The arc flash is also the game's loudest visual, which is why the cover screenshot shows one mid-flash.

gloworbs.role: Orbiting lanterns that circle the player and burn anything they touch — the close-range bodyguard.
gloworbs.stats: Level 1: 2 orbs, 10 damage per hit, 130 px orbit. Level 5: 5 orbs, 24 damage, 175 px orbit.
gloworbs.strategy: The best answer to being surrounded: the orbs clear the gloomlets that slip past the guns. Orbit radius grows with level, so high-level orbs let the player swim through a swarm and come out clean. Weak against spitters, who stay out of range.

ink_mines.role: Drifting mines the player drops behind them; they arm after a second and burst when an enemy comes close.
ink_mines.stats: Level 1: 1 mine every 2.4s, 34 damage in a 70 px burst. Level 5: 3 mines every 1.2s, 88 damage in a 130 px burst.
ink_mines.strategy: The kiting weapon: drop mines along your escape line and let the chase run into them. Splitters are the perfect mine food — the burst kills the parent and the children together. Mines persist 25 seconds, so a careful player can seed a whole quadrant.

pulse_ray.role: The starter weapon: a steady stream of cyan bolts at the nearest enemy.
pulse_ray.stats: Level 1: 8 damage, 3.2 shots/s. Level 5: 18 damage, 6.5 shots/s, pierce 2.
pulse_ray.strategy: Reliable single-target damage from the first second. Its level-5 pierce makes it a crowd weapon late, so it is never a dead pick — but it is the weakest against the Leviathan's bulk, so pair it with the harpoon or the storm.

sun_harpoon.role: The aimed heavy weapon: a golden harpoon that flies where the mouse points and pierces everything in its path.
sun_harpoon.stats: Level 1: 26 damage, 0.9 shots/s, pierce 1. Level 5: 62 damage, 1.7 shots/s, pierce 3.
sun_harpoon.strategy: The boss killer. Line the harpoon through a Leviathan and the pack behind it for full value; against a lone dart it is overkill. The only weapon the player aims, so it rewards mouse skill directly.
